excerpts.text:
[Apple](https://www.apple.com/)’s iPhone 17 is reportedly seeing strong demand on its first day of availability.

The latest generation of the iPhone lineup, including [iPhone 17](https://www.apple.com/iphone-17/), [iPhone Air](https://www.apple.com/iphone-air/), [iPhone 17 Pro](https://www.apple.com/iphone-17-pro/) and [iPhone 17 Pro Max](https://www.apple.com/iphone-17-pro/), launched in Apple Store locations worldwide as well as online and in the Apple Store app Friday (Sept. 19), according to a company [announcement](https://www.apple.com/newsroom/2025/09/the-latest-iphone-apple-watch-and-airpods-arrive-in-apple-store-locations/).

[JPMorgan](https://www.jpmorganchase.com/) increased its price target for Apple from $255 to $280, maintained its Overweight rating, and raised its revenue and earnings per share estimates, with analysts saying that the early demand indications suggest sales volumes will track higher than their initial expectations, Seeking Alpha [reported](https://seekingalpha.com/news/4496546-indicators-show-consumer-appetite-for-apples-iphone-17-stronger-than-expected-jp-morgan-raises-targets) Friday.

The report also quoted [Morgan Stanley](https://www.morganstanley.com/) saying Wednesday (Sept. 17) that “lead time analysis suggests that early demand for the iPhone 17 models is stronger than at the onset of the iPhone 16 cycle last year, a positive early indication that iPhone replacement cycles could be stabilizing and upgrade rates could be improving.”

The new iPhone lineup became available for preorders Sept. 12, and on that day, Chinese eCommerce platform [JD.com](https://corporate.jd.com/home) saw more of the iPhone 17 sold in the first minute of preorder than it saw of the iPhone 16 on that device’s first full day, CNBC [reported](https://www.cnbc.com/2025/09/19/apple-iphone-17-launch-sale-globally-china-market-and-ai-strategy.html) Friday.

Global demand for the new iPhone has also been positive, [Omdia](https://omdia.tech.informa.com/) Research Manager [Le Xuan Chiew](https://sg.linkedin.com/in/chiew-le-xuan-ab1a87179) told CNBC, citing preorder times and consumer feedback.

Apple's earnings for the quarter that ended in September met analysts' expectations on revenue but slightly missed on iPhone sales.iPhone sales in the fourth quarter were $49 billion, up from $46.2 billion compared to the same period ayear ago but slightly lower than the $50.1 billion Wall Street was expecting. Overall revenue was $102.5 billion, an increase from $94.9 billion a year ago.

Apple says both revenue and iPhone salesnumbers represent a record for the fourthquarter. Services revenue, another closely watched metric**,** also hit anall-time record at $28.8 billion, an increase from roughly $25 billion a year ago.
